Loss-of-function mutations in SLC26A4 lead to impaired sulfate transport and metabolism, affecting inner ear function and causing hearing impairment. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in SLC26A2 impair sulfate transport and metabolism, specifically impacting chondroitin sulfate biosynthesis, which is critical for cartilage and bone development, leading to skeletal dysplasia. The convergence lies in the shared role of sulfate transport and metabolism, with SLC26A2 more directly involved in the downstream biosynthesis of proteoglycans like chondroitin sulfate, which are important for skeletal development, while SLC26A4's role is more broadly in sulfate homeostasis which affects multiple tissues including the inner ear.
